newsitem.title: USA: CME pork bellies rally limit up late on buy stops.
newsitem.headline: CME pork bellies rally limit up late on buy stops.

text.p: CME pork belly futures shot up for a limit gain of 3.000 cents a lb in the March contract and ended sharply higher after short covering triggered fund buy stops. Hogs ended mostly up following bellies, traders said.

Pork bellies settled 2.775 to 1.000 cent higher paced by March at 78.525 cents. March touched limit up in the closing range and was limit bid in the post close. Hog futures ended 0.025 cent lower to 0.625 higher with only February down and April up 0.575 at 74.425 cents.
Late local short covering and persistent commercial buying boosted pork bellies into fund buy stops.

Bellies had traded in a wide range early with selling interest abating after a midsession break. The persistent light commercial buying then prompted locals to cover shorts which set off the buy stops late and prices rose as much as 4.000 cents from lows. Traders noted no fundamental reason for the surge but felt the market was oversold after recent sharp losses and due for a correction.

Floor sources cited talk that someone may be ready to stop deliveries. There have been more than expected deliveries against the February contract and talk of a strong stopper stepping in made shorts nervous, they said.
Chuck Levitt, senior livestock analyst for Alaron Trading Corp, noted that there are bellies in storage, but there are not a lot of those bellies certified to be deliverable.
"If someone wants to step in and stop 100 or 200 loads of bellies that would make it very dificult for shorts to line that (product) up," Levitt said.
R.J. O'Brien was a buyer much of the day with ABN Chicogo Corp a notable buyer in March and May late and Smith Barney a buyer in May late, pit sources said.
Hog futures generally rallied along with pork bellies with local short covering touching off buy stops, traders said.

Expectations that cash hog and pork prices are near a bottom provided underlying support although the still-weak tone to cash pork products kept a lid on February. Trade in February was also influenced by nervous action ahead of its expiration on Friday, they said.

February is the first lean contract to reach expiration and the industry wants to see how it adjusts to the lean hog index. Also, there are no trading limits in February the last two trading days, sources noted.
Rosenthal Collins and Rand Financials were on both sides of April during the day, pit sources said.

In hog options, trading remained slow with 71 to 73 puts offered in April early and locals selling February 76 calls late. Lind-Waldock sold out-of-the-money April puts and calls late, pit sources added.
